## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Is production ready to be deployed to? Reads only — creates nothing, changes nothing,
# safe to run any number of times.
#
# Run it while working through the provisioning checklist (issue #27) to see what is
# still missing, and run it first when a deploy fails, because most deploy failures are
# a resource or a secret that is not there.
name: preflight

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      stage:
        description: 'Which checks to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options: [all, resources, serving]

jobs:
  preflight:
    name: does production exist
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
      CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
      API_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.API_ORIGIN }}
      SITE_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.SITE_ORIGIN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Preflight
        run: |
          if [ "${{ inputs.stage }}" = "all" ]; then
            npm run preflight
          else
            npm run preflight -- --stage "${{ inputs.stage }}"
          fi

# hitbut's own build: the requirements suite, and the deploy that ships `main`.
name: product

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: product-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  checks:
    name: requirements (logic, behavior, server)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      # Watch the count, not the colour: a run that finds no tests exits green.
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run test:server
      # Phase 0's exit condition that needs no account: the committed wrangler.toml
      # builds and its bindings resolve.
      - run: npx wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/dry-run"

  screen:
    name: requirements (screen)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Pinned to the Playwright the goldens were rendered with. A different build
    # rasterises text differently, and the comparison would measure the renderer.
    container: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.56.1-noble
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run test:screen
      - name: The pictures, when they disagree
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: screen-failures
          path: dev/requirements/failures/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  deploy:
    name: ship main
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    needs: [checks, screen]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
      CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - name: Is there an account to deploy to yet?
        id: account
        run: |
          if [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ]; then
            echo "Cloudflare provisioning (issue #27) has not landed — nothing to deploy yet."
            echo "ready=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "ready=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm ci
      # Turns "the deploy failed somewhere in wrangler" into a named missing resource.
      # Only the resources stage: the origins cannot exist before the first deploy has
      # happened, so gating on them here would deadlock.
      - name: Does production exist?
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run preflight -- --stage resources
      - name: Bring the corpus schema up to date
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run corpus:migrate:remote
      - name: Deploy the Worker
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run deploy:api
      - name: Build the site against the deployed API
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        env:
          VITE_API_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.API_ORIGIN }}
          SITE_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.SITE_ORIGIN }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$VITE_API_ORIGIN" ] || [ -z "$SITE_ORIGIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::API_ORIGIN and SITE_ORIGIN must both be set as repository variables."
            echo "::error::This is expected on the very first deploy: the Worker above has just been"
            echo "::error::deployed and the site has not, so neither origin existed until now. Copy both"
            echo "::error::in and re-run this workflow — see the two-pass section of issue #27."
            exit 1
          fi
          npm run build:site
      - name: Deploy the site
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run deploy:site
      # Everything the suite proves is proven against a local workerd. This is the only
      # step that reads what actually shipped.
      - name: Does what shipped answer?
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        env:
          API_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.API_ORIGIN }}
          SITE_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.SITE_ORIGIN }}
        run: npm run smoke

Short answer: **no.** Section A is genuinely human-only. Almost nothing else is.

I verified the create commands against the wrangler actually pinned in this repo (`npm ci` + `--help`, no network), not from memory:

| #27 step | Reality |
|---|---|
| B — D1 `hitbut-corpus` | `wrangler d1 create hitbut-corpus` — positional name, every flag optional. Non-interactive. |
| B — R2 `hitbut-raw` | `wrangler r2 bucket create hitbut-raw` — same. |
| B — Queue `hitbut-analysis` | `wrangler queues create hitbut-analysis` — same. |
| B — Vectorize | `wrangler vectorize create hitbut-utterances --dimensions N --metric cosine` (or `--preset`). The *model choice* is a human decision; the creation is not. |
| B — Pages project `hitbut` | `wrangler pages project create hitbut --production-branch main`. The issue's stated reason ("a non-interactive runner cannot answer a prompt") is exactly what `--production-branch` removes. |
| C — paste `database_id` | `wrangler d1 create` takes `--update-config --binding CORPUS` and writes the id into `wrangler.toml` itself. A provisioning job can open that PR. |

All of them take the **same token section A already produces**. So the checklist's premise — "every step here needs the Cloudflare dashboard or the repo's secret store" — holds for A and for essentially nothing after it.

Three further problems I found while checking:

1. **Two steps may not exist at all.** "Enable Workers AI" and "Enable Workflows" are listed as account clicks. As far as I know neither is a toggle — the binding is the enablement. I could **not** verify this: `developers.cloudflare.com` is egress-blocked from this sandbox (`EGRESS_BLOCKED`, domain-wide), so this needs a human or an unblocked environment to confirm before either line is trusted.

2. **The issue's factual claim about `wrangler.toml` is wrong.** It says the queue is "producer + consumer, both already in `wrangler.toml`", and names bindings `AI` and `VECTORS`. `wrangler.toml` contains **only** D1, R2, the cron trigger and `[vars]` — no queues, no AI, no Vectorize, no Workflows. Those four are blocked on **#34's code**, not on the account; `src/backend/ingestion/unprovisioned.ts` is the placeholder. Listing them under "create the resources" makes the human's blocking list look twice as long as it is.

3. **The two-pass first deploy in E is probably avoidable too.** The Pages production origin is deterministic (`https://hitbut.pages.dev`), and the Worker's is `https://hitbut-api.<workers.dev subdomain>.workers.dev`, which the account API can answer. Deriving both and feeding them straight into `build:site` removes the `API_ORIGIN`/`SITE_ORIGIN` repository-variable step *and* the deliberate first-pass failure. Less certain than the rest — the subdomain lookup is the part I'd have to prove.

Realistically the human list collapses to: pick account → mint token → paste two secrets → run one workflow. Roughly four items instead of fifteen.

# Creates whatever production is missing, in the Cloudflare account the repository secrets
# point at. Deliberately a button rather than part of the deploy: creating resources spends
# money in someone's account, which is a decision, where deploying to resources that already
# exist is not.
#

# a partial run, or after adding a scope to the token, is the normal way to use it.
name: provision

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dry_run:
        description: 'Only say what would be created'
        type: boolean
        default: false

# The database id D1 hands out is the one piece of production that lives in the repo.
permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  provision:
    name: create what is missing
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
      CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
      # A Vectorize index fixes its dimensions at creation, so it is created only once the
      # embedding model is chosen (#34) and this variable says what it outputs.
      VECTORIZE_DIMENSIONS: ${{ vars.VECTORIZE_DIMENSIONS }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - name: Are there credentials to provision with?
        run: |
          if [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ]; then
            echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN must both be set as repository"
            echo "::error::secrets before anything can be created. They are the only part of provisioning"
            echo "::error::that needs a person — see issue #27."
            exit 1
          fi
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Create what is missing
        run: npm run provision ${{ inputs.dry_run && '-- --dry-run' || '' }}
      # The id is generated data, not a decision: whatever D1 handed out is the only correct
      # value, so it goes straight to main rather than through a review it cannot fail.
      - name: Pin the database id on main
        if: ${{ !inputs.dry_run }}
        run: |
          if git diff --quiet -- wrangler.toml; then
            echo "wrangler.toml already carries the real database id — nothing to commit."
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add wrangler.toml
          git commit -m "Pin the provisioned D1 database id

          if ! git push origin HEAD:main; then

            echo "::error::below; commit it by hand and the deploy will work."
            git --no-pager diff HEAD~1 -- wrangler.toml
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Where production now stands
        if: always()
        run: npm run preflight || true

calls against a corpus meant to hold decades, it needs a topic vocabulary to

statements are where a trend lives. The pairwise page survives as a *view*: the

deploy rather than after: the window the three-step discipline protects is
between applying migrations and replacing the running Worker, and there was no
running Worker to protect. Detection is pure code over a stance series now, so

Only findings above a surfacing threshold reach the product; the full
distribution is kept for tuning. The model call sits behind one interface, so
moving to a different model or an external provider is a config change rather
than a rewrite.

## HTTP API

Read-only public JSON under a versioned path (`/api/v1/...`): personas, a
persona's timeline, utterance detail with its attestations, findings, and
search. Cursor pagination, open CORS, no accounts, no write surface — the only
writers are the cron trigger and the backfill's Workflow. Responses
are edge-cacheable with short TTLs; bulk export is served as generated snapshots
from R2 rather than paginated through D1.

## Frontend

A static site on Cloudflare Pages — no Pages Functions, no server rendering:
everything the site shows is public and comes from `/api/v1`, so the API stays
the one back end and the front end stays a pile of cacheable assets. Page
inventory: home (search + recent findings), persona (profile, timeline,
findings), utterance detail (text, attestations, sources), finding detail (the
utterances side by side with rationale and sources), search results, and a
methodology page explaining how detection works and how to report an error.

## How requirements are proven against this

Data-level requirements (extraction, corpus invariants, ingestion, analysis)
assert on values directly, with committed real sample payloads as fixtures, and
with the model and the vector store behind interfaces a case can script. UI
requirements drive this front end in headless Chromium against a local
`wrangler` preview of the real deployment, asserting on committed screenshot
goldens — the harness runs what ships, not a mock shell.

input.title: Create production from a workflow instead of a checklist
input.body:
Most of what #27 lists as human-only isn't. Every resource the account needs is one non-interactive `wrangler … create`, and both deploy origins are knowable the moment their half is deployed — so neither the per-resource dashboard clicking nor the deliberate two-pass first deploy was ever necessary.

What genuinely needs a person: **pick the account, mint the API token, paste the two secrets** — and press the button that says yes, spend money in that account. That's it.

### `provision`, a new workflow

Creates whatever the preflight reports missing, from the same table the preflight reads, so the two cannot disagree about what production is. Idempotent — re-running after a partial run, or after widening the token, is the normal way to use it.

Two refusals it will not break, both held by the gate:

* **Only on a confirmed absence.** A resource we could *not ask about* — a token scope, a renamed command, a refused network — is left alone and reported. Creating a second copy of something already there is worse than stopping.
* **Never a shape that cannot be changed later.** A Vectorize index fixes its dimensions at creation, so without an explicit `VECTORIZE_DIMENSIONS` it declines rather than pick one (waits on the embedding model, #34).

It also reads the D1 id back and commits it to `main` — generated data, not a decision, and the deploy is gated on it anyway.

### The first deploy is a single pass

`deploy.ts` deploys one half and reads its origin back: the Worker's out of what `wrangler deploy` printed, the site's off the Pages project itself (the deployment alias is a URL that answers but isn't where anyone reads the site). Each origin is exported for the next step, so the site builds against the API that was just deployed and the smoke test knows where to look. `API_ORIGIN` / `SITE_ORIGIN` survive as overrides for a custom domain — the one thing that can't be derived — rather than as something the first deploy needs.

That removes section E of #27 entirely: the deliberate first-pass failure, the two repository variables, and the manual re-run.

### Verified

`npm test` (78), `npm run test:server` (13), `npm run typecheck`, `wrangler deploy --dry-run` all green. The new gate was watched failing first — four cases red when `decide` was made to create on an unknown, when `--production-branch` was dropped, and when the site-origin fallback stopped stripping the deployment label; a fifth when `jsonArrayIn` was reduced to the first `[` (wrangler's own `[WARNING]` line). `npm run preflight` and `npm run provision -- --dry-run` were both run credential-less here: every check reports `??`, and provisioning declines all five items rather than create anything.

What can't be verified from a session is the half that needs an account — the actual creates, and the origins as wrangler really prints them. #30 already watches for that.

`.github/workflows` — new `provision` workflow; `preflight` loses its now-empty stage input; `product`'s deploy job drops the deliberate first-pass failure and threads the derived origins between its steps.
`dev/tools` — new `cloudflare.ts` (the resource table, the wrangler runner, and the create/leave decision), `provision.ts`, `deploy.ts`, `origins.ts`; `preflight.ts` rewritten to read the shared table and to name the fix for each miss.
`dev/gates` — new `provisioning.test.ts`, holding the two refusals and the origin reading.

Refs #27

Production only: local development and the whole test suite run against wrangler's local D1/R2 and need none of this. **Rewritten 2026-08-23.** This list used to be nine dashboard steps and a two-pass first deploy. Most of that was never necessary — every resource is one non-interactive `wrangler … create`, and both deploy origins are readable off the deploys themselves. #69 landed the automation. What is left is three pastes and two buttons. **You never have to guess whether a step worked.** After each one run **[preflight](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/workflows/preflight.yml)** → *Run workflow*. It reads production and changes nothing, so run it as often as you like, and it names what is still missing and how to fix it. It is also the first thing to run if a deploy fails. Read its output carefully: `MISS` means Cloudflare says the resource is not there, `??` means the question could not be asked at all (usually a token scope). They need opposite fixes — and the provisioner declines to create anything on a `??` for exactly that reason. --- ## A. The part that needs a person - [ ] **Pick the Cloudflare account** and copy its Account ID — [dash.cloudflare.com](https://dash.cloudflare.com/) → any domain or *Workers & Pages*; the ID is in the right-hand sidebar (and it is the hex string in the dashboard URL, `dash.cloudflare.com//…`). - [ ] **Create a scoped API token** — [dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens](https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens) → *Create Token* → *Create Custom Token*. Permissions: *Workers Scripts: Edit*, *D1: Edit*, *Workers R2 Storage: Edit*, *Queues: Edit*, *Cloudflare Pages: Edit*, *Vectorize: Edit*, *Workers AI: Read*. Copy it once — it is not shown again. - [ ] **Paste both as repository secrets** — [Settings → Secrets → Actions](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/settings/secrets/actions) → *New repository secret*, named exactly `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`.
*While off:* the deploy job detects the missing credentials, says so, and exits clean. Nothing below can happen either — everything needs the token. ## B. Press the button - [ ] **Run [provision](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/workflows/provision.yml)** → *Run workflow*. It creates every resource that is missing and leaves alone every one that is already there, so re-running it is safe and is the normal way to finish a partial run. It creates: the **D1 database** `hitbut-corpus` (the corpus — every API route needs it), the **R2 bucket** `hitbut-raw` (raw payloads, and the bulk export; without it a parser fix would need a re-fetch), and the **Pages project** `hitbut` (there is no site otherwise). It then reads the database id back out of D1 and commits it to `main`, which is the one piece of production that lives in the repo. It deliberately does **not** create the **Vectorize index** yet: an index fixes its dimension count at creation and the embedding model is not chosen (#34). Choose the model, set a `VECTORIZE_DIMENSIONS` [repository variable](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/settings/variables/actions) to what it outputs, and re-run this workflow. Until then, ingestion has no retrieval step and the Worker's ports fail by name rather than silently doing nothing. It is a button rather than part of the deploy because creating resources spends money in your account. That decision is yours; the clicking is not. ## C. Gate, then ship - [ ] **Run [preflight](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/workflows/preflight.yml) and get it green.** The deploy runs the same check before it touches anything, so a green preflight is the difference between a first deploy that works and one that fails halfway through having already deployed the Worker. - [ ] **Let a merge to `main` deploy.** The provisioner's own commit is enough. One pass: preflight → migrations → Worker → site built against the origin the Worker just reported → site deployed → smoke test against both. No human step, which is requirement `7.1`. A custom domain in front of either half is the only thing that cannot be derived — set `API_ORIGIN` / `SITE_ORIGIN` as [repository variables](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/settings/variables/actions) if you put one there, and they win. ## Not steps, contrary to what this issue used to say - **Queue `hitbut-analysis`** — the queue was dropped in the redesign (#59); nothing binds one. - **Workers AI, Workflows** — neither has a binding in `wrangler.toml` today, so neither blocks anything until #34 lands the code that uses them. Whether either needs an account-level enable at all is **unverified** — the sandbox this was written in cannot reach Cloudflare's docs. Check it when #34 gets there rather than trusting the old checklist. Note on models: the redesign needs **two** model calls of different shapes — an embedding model (one vector per utterance, high volume, cheap) and a stance model (one judgment per utterance, low volume, needs real Hebrew competence). They may not come from the same provider, and #28's item 3 — Hebrew competence unevaluated — applies to the second. **Closes when** the `product` workflow on `main` is green end to end — smoke test included — and one merge is observed reaching the deployed site with no human build step. #30 checks for exactly that and reports back on its own. Refs #25, #34, #36, #38, #69
